terms.meaning: a framework for building websites and web apps with React
a library for building page parts that update on screen
a frame that wraps and stays around the page content
a wrapper that makes shared data available to the pages inside it
a shared store of data that a provider passes down to components
a set of letter shapes used for text on the page
page details such as the title and description that browsers and search engines read

used_by: Every page in src/app, applied automatically by Next.js (no importing file is visible)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and font setup
sections.what: Loads the framework, the stylesheets, the shared providers and the app shell, and sets up four fonts the site uses.
sections.why: Fonts are declared once here so every page can use them.
sections.watch_out: Adding or removing a font weight here changes what is downloaded.

sections.name: metadata, viewport
sections.title: Page title and screen settings
sections.what: Sets the browser tab title and its template for other pages, the search description, and a phone-friendly screen setting.
sections.why: Gives every page a consistent title and description.
sections.watch_out: The description is public wording that search results may show, so edits affect what people see.

sections.name: RootLayout
sections.title: Outer page frame
sections.what: Builds the outer html element with the font classes and a body that holds the providers and the app shell around the page content.
sections.why: Next.js needs this outermost component to wrap every page.
sections.watch_out: Nesting order is LocaleProvider, then CaseProvider, then AppShell. Changing it can break parts that need one of them.

summary: Root frame for every page: loads fonts and stylesheets, sets the page title and description, and wraps the app in the language and case providers and the app shell.
purpose: Provides the shared outer frame that every page sits inside.
why: Next.js needs one root layout, and this file serves that role. The code does not state other reasons for the structure.
how: Loads four Google fonts with a swap display setting. Imports the styling files. Sets the page metadata and viewport. Renders the html element with the font class names, then wraps the page content in LocaleProvider, CaseProvider and AppShell.
inputs: The page content passed in by Next.js. Font files fetched through next/font/google at build time.
outputs: A complete HTML page with fonts, styles, the app shell and the page content inside.
risks: Font downloads happen at build time, so a failed font download can stop the build. The provider nesting order matters, and changing it can break components that need one of the providers.
debug: If styling is missing, check the imports at the top of the file. If fonts look wrong, check the font variable names on the html element. If every page is blank, check the providers and AppShell.
